items.explanation: きゃ is 'kya': き ('ki') plus a small ゃ ('ya'), said as one beat. A combination is an i-column kana followed by a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ, and the two are said together as ONE beat. Size matters: きや (full-size や) is two beats, ki-ya, while きゃ (small ゃ) is one beat, kya.
items.mnemonic: The big き swallows the little ゃ: 'ki' and 'ya' squeeze into one beat, 'kya'.
items.culture_note: Shop staff greet customers with いらっしゃいませ (irasshaimase, 'welcome'), and a customer is politely called おきゃくさま (okyakusama).
